newsitem.title: GERMANY: Individuals should avoid Telekom shares - advisor.
newsitem.headline: Individuals should avoid Telekom shares - advisor.

text.p: Individual investors should proceed cautiously on soon-to-be-offered shares in Deutsche Telekom AG, the Society for the Protection of Small Investors (SdK) said on Thursday.
"The initial price will likely be much too high. Telekom will have trouble maintaining it," SdK Director Anneliese Hieke told German radio.

The German state telephone monopoly will make an initial public offering on November 18. The issue is expected to be slightly over 15 percent of Telekom's shares, raising an estimated 15 billion marks ($9.9 billion).
Telekom will have to cut rates by up to 60 percent to prepare itself for full competition in 1998, Hieke said. She advised investors to wait for a fall from the initial price before buying.
Hieke said Commerzbank AG's offer to guarantee the Telekom price was counterproductive, and she could not recommend it.
Commerzbank has merely offered to return to investors in 2002 the same amount they invested in 1996, while it receives all tax credits and dividends for the shares.

"In that case I would simply advise people to buy fixed-income securities, for example Post bonds that now pay 7.19 percent. Compared to that one can see that Telekom shares are mainly designed to pay off Telekom's debts."
Telekom in August took steps to woo small investors by offering up to 300 shares at a reduced rate of 10,000 marks, for an implied stock price of 33 marks.
Brokerage Barclays de Zoete Wedd, which is not part of the underwriting group, has also said Telekom's estimate was too high.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49 228 26097150 ($ = 1.509 German Marks)
